subject: Discrepancy in hyperparameter fitting behavior for two gaussian process ensemble models

messages.author: 88be8046d498a27b
messages.subject: Discrepancy in hyperparameter fitting behavior for two gaussian process ensemble models
parts:
Below are two STAN models for fitting the length-scale hyperparameters of an ensemble of 10 independent gaussian processes with identical inputs x but distinct responses y_i. The first model samples from

p( l_i | y_i, x)

where l_i is the vector of length scale hyperparameters for GP i, y_i is the vector of training observations for GP i, and x is the matrix of input parameters that is the same for all GPs in the ensemble.

The second model samples from

p( l | y, x ),

where l is the matrix of length-scale hyper parameters for all GPs in the ensemble, and y is the matrix of all training observations in the ensemble.

Since each GP in the ensemble is independent, the marginal posterior for length-scale hyperparameter vector i should be equivalent for both models:

p(l_i | y_i, x) = p(l_i | y, x).

However, in practice, the first model converges after a relatively short time, whereas the second model runs much more slowly and does not converge. Can anyone comment on this discrepancy? I’ve included some sample data for each model in rdump format. x and y are both scaled to have 0 mean and unit variance.

Thanks,
Danny

Model 1:
data {
  int T; // number of training points in the ensemble
  int V; // dimensionality of input space
  vector[V] x[T]; // inputs
  vector[T] y; // responses
  real<lower=0> nug;
}

transformed data {
  vector[T] mu;
  for (i in 1:T)
    mu[i] <- 0;
}

parameters {
  vector<lower=0>[V] l;
}

model {
  matrix[T, T] Sigma;
  for (j in 1:T-1){
    for (k in j+1:T){
      Sigma[j, k] <- exp(-dot_self((x[j] - x[k]) ./ l));
      Sigma[k, j] <- Sigma[j, k];
    }
  }
  for (j in 1:T)
    Sigma[j, j] <- 1 + nug;
  l ~ student_t(4,0,1);
  y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

Model 2:

data {
  int N; // number of gps in the ensemble
  int T; // number of training points in the ensemble
  int V; // dimensionality of input space
  vector[V] x[T]; // input parameters
  vector[T] y[N]; // observations
  real<lower=0> nug;
}

transformed data {
  vector[T] mu;
  for (i in 1:T)
    mu[i] <- 0;
}

parameters {
  vector<lower=0>[V] l[N];
}

model {
  matrix[T, T] Sigma[N];
  for (i in 1:N){
    for (j in 1:T-1){
      for (k in j+1:T){
Sigma[i, j, k] <- exp(-dot_self((x[j] - x[k]) ./ l[i]));
Sigma[i, k, j] <- Sigma[i, j, k];
      }
    }
    for (j in 1:T)
      Sigma[i, j, j] <- 1 + nug;
    l[i] ~ student_t(4,0,1);
    y[i] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma[i]);
  }
}

I understand GPs, but all I can say is that Model 2 uses more memory, which may make it slower, but there is also something going wrong in Model 2 as the lp__ for Model 2 gets ridiculous values. My guess is that this is an initialization problem. It would be good to test by initializing the parameters to exactly same values in both models.

Aki
